newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PAL plans to convert A300-B4s to freighters.
newsitem.headline: PAL plans to convert A300-B4s to freighters.

text.p: Philippine Airlines is seeking board approval to convert two of its ageing Airbus A300-B4 passenger aircraft into domestic and regional freighters, the airline's senior vice president for sales and service, Avelino Zapanta, told Reuters.
PAL is also in the early stages of talks with prospective partners to operate freighter services to Europe and the U.S..
Negotiations are being held with Cargolux and Lufthansa Cargo about a European cargo link from Manila.
Atlas Air has been approached about wet-leasing a Boeing 747-200 freighter for a trans-Pacific cargo service possibly in co-operation with two other carriers, Zapanta added.
PAL, Indonesian flag carrier Garuda and Continental Airlines are interested in a Jakarta, Manila, Guam, Honolulu to west coast U.S. cargo operation.
"We are just at the talking stage and nothing is definite yet," Zapanta said in an interview.

Part of PAL's revival plan is to concentrate more on cargo and raise its share of total revenue from the present 10 percent. The need for a dedicated freighter service has been highlighted by the arrival of a new fleet of Airbus A340, A330 and, from next week, A320, aircraft.

Airbus A340-300 aircraft which have replaced Boeing 747s on PAL services to London and Frankfurt has severely affected cargo uplift, Zapanta said. Unlike PAL's 747 "milk run" services via Bangkok and Abu Dhabi, the new A340s are flying non-stop but the ultra long-haul means reduced cargo payload, he said.
"The A340 is very good for our passenger marketing but the non-stop service means cargo is payload restricted in both directions," Zapanta said.

PAL has also identified a need for a domestic and regional freighter service. Zapanta said he is confident of board approval for the conversion into freighters of two of the airline's elderly A300-B4 regional and domestic workhorses.

"We have just had the final meeting with various operations units to finalise the paperwork and hope to present the final study to the management board next week. We are very confident that the B4 conversion programme will be approved and enter service later this year," Zapanta said.
